subject: Sprint zero: compact on-prem cluster — node classes, IO guardrails & operator handshake
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@orbhealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: SiteOps <siteops@orbhealth.com>; procurement@orbhealth.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 13:03:00 -0400
Subject: Sprint zero - compact footprint for OrbHealth private deploy

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the quick sync earlier. We want to proceed with a sprint-zero for a compact on-prem cluster in our primary datacenter (single-rack target). High-level constraints:
- Single rack, 10U reserved for the cluster (tight RV space).
- Two failure domains only (A/B rack-level power feeds).
- Goal: host inference serving (small RD throughput), model caching, and lightweight control plane services.

Questions we need help on from Redwood:
1) Recommended node classes (cpu-only infra, small-gpu for prod, burst-gpu) and a minimal sizing suggestion.
2) Persistent storage options: local NVMe ephemeral for inference KV cache + small blockstore for long-lived artifacts. Any preferences on CSI or operators?
3) Network/VLAN guidance — we have one public uplink and private VLANs; we need VLAN maps and MTU guidance.
4) Operator / onboarding checklist (what we need to hand to our SiteOps folks).

Can you send a compact plan and a short checklist we can hand to our team? I've attached the facility inventory (small) and a rough rack diagram.

Attachments: orbhealth-sprint0-inventory-request.csv, rack-sketch.png (not attached here)

Appreciate it — Liam

Liam / SiteOps — thanks for the inventory and constraints. Quick reply with a compact, runnable plan and an action checklist attached (sprint-zero-checklist.pdf). Summary below so you can share with the on-site team: 

1) Node classes (minimal, targeted at single-rack footprint):
  - control-plane: 3 x m.2 NVMe boot nodes (small CPU) running control plane components; prefer dedicated small instances so API is stable. Recommend 3x for quorum even in constrained footprint.
  - infra (system services + observability): 2 x cpu-large (32 vCPU / 128GB) with 2 x 1TB NVMe for logs + admin workloads. Run logging/monitoring with retention folded into central object store.
  - workload-cpu: 3 x cpu-medium (16 vCPU / 64GB) for non-GPU inference, batch conversions, and webhooks.
  - workload-gpu-prod: 2 x gpu-small (A2-style / 1x 80GB GPU equivalent) — primary inference workers.
  - workload-gpu-burst: 1 x gpu-burst (smaller card or shared card via device plugin) to absorb spikes.

Notes: we intentionally keep the control plane separate; even in a cramped rack, 3 control-plane nodes are important to avoid split-brain during maintenance. If rack space is more constrained, consider a 2-control-plane + managed-control-plane hybrid — we can discuss.

2) Storage & IO guardrails:
  - Ephemeral NVMe: use for inference KV cache (prefix cache + KV cache) and local model shards. Mount as fast ephemeral storage and expose via HostPath/LocalPV (CSI local-static or local-volume provisioner).
  - Blockstore (object-backed): long-lived artifacts (snapshots, model binaries) should go to an external block/object system accessible over private VLAN (we'll use s3-compatible object store).
  - PVC classes:
    * local-ephemeral: hostPath/LocalPV, fast NVMe, no replication (best for cache).
    * block-primary: network-attached block via CSI (replicated), for DBs and persistent checkpoints.
    * archive-object: s3-compatible for artifacts and logs.
  - IO guardrails: define pod QoS and I/O throttling via cgroups and kubernetes resource limits (io.kubernetes). Enforce eviction thresholds at 80% disk to avoid OOM/evictions during heavy writes.

3) Network guidance:
  - MTU: set to 9000 (jumbo frames) between nodes and uplink where possible; fallback 1500 if the facility network doesn't support it.
  - VLAN plan (draft attached network-vlan-draft.yaml):
    * management-vlan: kube-apiserver, etcd replication traffic (isolated).
    * data-vlan: workload traffic, model pulls, object-store egress.
    * storage-vlan: blockstore and NFS (if used).
    * out-of-band: out-of-band management for IPMI/iLO.
  - Egress: use a small number of NAT IPs for model downloads; recommend a caching proxy for model blobs (reduces repeated egress and speeds pulls).

4) Operator / onboarding handshake (what SiteOps needs):
  - K8s version: 1.25+ (we'll provide tested image matrix).
  - CSI drivers: CSI for blockstore + local-static provisioner.
  - Device plugins: NVIDIA or equivalent for GPUs; test device plugin on a single node before fleet rollout.
  - KMS access: customer-managed KMS endpoint + cert for key unwrap. Provide key wrap steps.
  - Component images: list of images and sha256 we will deploy (included in sprint-zero checklist).

Action items for SiteOps (short):
  - Confirm available VLANs and MTU support (due: Tue 2026-06-16).
  - Provide serial numbers and NIC details for candidate nodes (we'll map nodeclasses).
  - Validate external object store connectivity and egress rules.

Attachments included: sprint-zero-checklist.pdf (action checklist), network-vlan-draft.yaml (VLAN/MTU draft). Also attaching a one-page runbook-stub for operator handshake.

I'll loop Karthik for sizing and Monica for the runbook. If you want, we can convert the checklist into a HubSpot playbook for tracking acceptance criteria.

Thanks,
Neha

Quick clarifications from sizing side — flagged items we should lock before we create the final BOM: 

- GPU sizing: suggest 2x prod GPUs (as Neha suggested) but pick cards with at least 48GB VRAM if you plan to host bigger LLM shards. If the workload is single smaller models, a 24–40GB card may suffice and will free rack power.
- Autoscaling & burst: with only one rack, consider node-level pod-Autoscaler + cluster-level manual burst node (gpu-burst) to avoid noisy neighbor issues. Add an admission control that prevents large bulk jobs from starting during peak hours.
- Disk IO: for the local-ephemeral class, recommend fio baseline measurement during site validation — we need sustained 1GB/s per NVMe during warm model loads. If the NVMe is < 3GB/s, we will plan to split workloads across more nodes.
- PV binding: use local-static CSI for local NVMe to avoid double-scheduling issues — we should include static PV claims in the onboarding playbook.

I'll update the sprint-zero checklist with these sizing gates and include a short acceptance test (model-pull + 5 concurrent inference clients + KV cache warmup) that SiteOps can run.

- Karthik

Thanks — uploaded a short runbook-stub.md to the shared drive (link in metadata). A couple of practical ops notes I asked SiteOps about during the inventory review: 

- Power budgeting: confirm per-rack PDUs and whether any nodes share PDU strips; if there is a shared PDU we must schedule rolling updates to not hit a single PDU failure.
- BIOS settings: require AHCI for NVMe, disable C-state deep sleep for predictable latency, and ensure nvme_timeout is tuned per vendor.
- Time sync: prefer GPS/NTP redundancy — kubelet clock drift causes certificate renewals to fail in small clusters.

Action: Liam / SiteOps — can you confirm PDUs and BIOS baseline? If yes we'll push the runbook-stub as the first draft acceptance test and include the fio profile Karthik mentioned.

Attachments referenced: runbook-stub.md (outline), sprint-zero-checklist.pdf
